subject: POC qualification: success metrics, timeline, and owner roster
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kline <sarah.kline@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ethan Li <ethan.li@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + proposed POC success slate and owners

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed way forward so we have alignment before we lock dates.

Top takeaways from discovery:
- Primary workload: real-time multi-turn chat for customer support (English, US).
- Expected peak concurrency: ~40 simultaneous users during spikes; baseline 10–15.
- Latency sensitivity: perceived time-to-response under 300ms is ideal.
- Cost sensitivity: looking to validate sub-$0.0009/token economics on average workloads.

Proposed POC scope (4 weeks):
1) Goals and KPIs (what we will measure)
  - Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency <= 220ms for 1k token average context.
  - Throughput: sustain 50 RPS steady-state with <10% tail latency degradation.
  - Cost: average model cost <= $0.0008 per token (incl. caching and batching).
  - Quality: intent accuracy >= 92% on your 200-case validation set; hallucination rate < 2% on sensitive prompts.
2) Success evidence
  - Load-tested runbook artifacts, token-level cost report, sample transcripts, and automated eval results.
3) Ownership
  - Redwood: runtime setup, model variant tuning, load-run execution, cost report (Rishi + Ben).
  - Novacorp: provide sample prompt set, evaluation rubric, sandbox keys, and an ops contact for network/VPC testing (Ethan).
4) Timeline and cadence
  - Week 0 (prep): artifact handoff and sandbox access.
  - Week 1: baseline smoke + small-volume functional tests.
  - Week 2: scale tests and initial cost tuning.
  - Week 3: quality validation and guardrails.
  - Week 4: readout and decision.

Next steps I propose today:
- Novacorp provides sandbox API key and 200-case validation rubric by Fri 2026-12-03.
- Redwood shares POC checklist and cost estimate by EOD tomorrow (attached).
- Kickoff dry-run meeting Wed 2026-12-08 (30 min).

Attachment: novacorp-poc-checklist.pdf (checklist + minimal infra needs)

If this looks reasonable I'll loop Ben (engineering lead for POCs) and Marissa (Customer Success) to confirm operational roles.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

3) Timeline: can we shift the kickoff to Thu 2026-12-09? Our Ops lead (Ethan) will need a dry-run time where networking can be validated.

We will deliver the 200-case validation set and rubric by Friday. Also, can you confirm the estimated token spend ceiling for the POC so I can clear with procurement?

Thanks Sarah — great questions. Quick answers inline and updated POC ceiling below.

- Model-only latency: we'll report both model-only P95 and end-to-end P95. Target model-only P95 <= 160ms.
- Safety metric: we can add "response safety" with false-positive sensitive content flags <1% and harmful-generation rate <0.5% on your sensitive prompt subset.
- Kickoff: Thu 2026-12-09 works for us; propose 10:00 AM PT as a default.
- Token spend ceiling: we estimate a safe testing ceiling of 1.2M tokens for the 4-week POC. Estimated cost: $960 (based on conservative token-cost assumptions); we'll run daily burn-rate checks and throttle tests if needed. Detailed numbers attached (redwood-cost-estimates.xlsx).

Operational owners (updated):
- Redwood: Rishi (SE lead), Ben Carter (runtime & load), Marissa Cole (CS lead, readout & success rubric).
- Novacorp: Sarah (product owner), Ethan (ops/network), Platform team contact to be added for VPC peering.

Kickoff agenda (30 min):
- Introductions and goals (5m)
- Access and network checklist (10m)
- Smoke test plan and responsibilities (10m)
- Success evidence and readout timing (5m)

I'll attach the POC checklist and cost workbook now. Can you confirm Ethan's availability for the dry-run and if Novacorp needs an NDA or security addendum before sandbox access?

Cheers —
Rishi

Looping in engineering notes from my side — planning notes for the load run: 

1) Baseline infra we need from Novacorp:
  - Sandbox endpoint + scoped API key (rate-limited),
  - Optional VPC peering details if they want model hosted in their private deployment during last-week validation.
2) Load plan: ramp to 60 RPS in 10 minutes, hold for 30 minutes for stability, then drop to 20 RPS and run quality checks.
3) Caching: recommend enabling response prefix caching for high-similarity prompts; should cut token spend 10–18% depending on prompt reuse.
4) Measurement artifacts we will deliver:
  - Token-level cost CSV, per-route latency percentiles, sampling of transcripts with eval flags.

I'll take point on the load window and the daily burn report. Ben
